newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares listless in early bourse trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares listless in early bourse trade.

text.p: German shares were stronger in early bourse trade on Tuesday, but traders said market sentiment was nervous and expected any advances to be capped over the day.

The DAX index, which tracks bourse trade in 30 German blue-chips, was down 2.26 points at 3,762.85 points in early trade, a fall of 0.06 percent early on, while the June DAX futures contract was up 14.5 points at 3,762.5.

"It's steady to a fraction better today, and the dollar is helping. But there is a lot of nervousness around and a lot of it is related to the negotiations at the Amsterdam summit," said one trader of the European Union summit.
"A lot of the agreements in Amsterdam are being seen as posturing. It's all politics, and everyone thinks they are just trying to paper over the cracks in currency union," the trader said.
EU leaders, meeting in Amsterdam, on Monday agreed a resolution on employment to accompany the stability pact, the framework for keeping budgets tight under EMU.
While there was a lot of movement going on, most of it was based on derivatives.
"There is the triple-witching on Friday, and there are a lot of U.S. figures this week, but basically I think this market needs a rest," the trader said.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed slightly lower overnight, down 0.13 percent at 7,772.09 points.
While such an inconclusive figure did not have a major impact on sentiment in Frankfurt, it did not provide the same levels of impetus as it has done in recent days.

Schwarz Pharma was among the best performers in morning electronic trade after it received approval the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market its EDEX treatment for impotence in the United States.
Schwarz Pharma shares were up 6.40 marks, or 4.79 percent, at 139.90 marks in early bourse trade.
Other big losers in ealry bourse trade inlcuded Adidas, down nearly three percent at 197 marks and SGL Carbon down 2.38 percent at 236 marks.
Dealers said there were no major fundamental reasons behind the decline in the two stocks.
